recipes.name: Green Tomato Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (14 ounce) package double-crust pie pastry, thawed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine tomatoes and vinegar in a large bowl.
Mix sugar, flour, cinnamon, nutmeg, salt, and cloves together in a medium bowl. Sprinkle over tomatoes and toss to coat evenly.
Press one thawed pie crust into a 9-inch pie pan. Pour tomato mixture into the pastry. Cut second pie crust into strips and arrange in a crisscross lattice over the filling.
Bake in the preheated oven until filling is bubbly and crust is brown, 30 to 35 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Green Tomato Pie
raw_recipe.description: This green tomato pie, packed with chopped green tomatoes and sweetened with sugar and cinnamon, resembles the taste and texture of apple pie.

review.reviewBody: Wow! It really does taste like apple pie. I actually peeled the tomatoes (a knife worked easier than a veggie peeler for me) since that's what I do with apples. I upped the flour to about 1/3 cup and ended up baking it for an hour. It came out great- not too runny like some reviews said.

I made 3 small changes based on others' note that the pie has too much liquid. I added 2 tsp corn starch and upped the flour to about 1/3 c. After mixing the tomatoes sugar and vinegar, I scooped out as much of the liquid as was easily removable. Then when filling the pie shell, I put in all the tomatoes and enough liquid to come about half to 2/3 of the way up the walls of the shell.

Based on the last green tomato pie I made, I cut the tomatoes into wedges and then cut the wedges into thirds crosswise, so I didn't end up with large hunks of hard tomato.

Delicious pie.

This is very good! Tastes just like apple pie. I used green Roma and Cherry tomatoes. I didn't have cider vinegar, so I added a bit of chopped apple and regular vinegar. I also added a smidge more flour, and cooked down the filling on the stove until thick before baking. I definitely can see how this would have been super runny otherwise. Highly recommend cooking it down beforehand!

I was juggling some other baking and wasn't able to assemble the pie immediately after mixing up the filling. The filling became very juicy, so I scooped out the tomatoes and cooked the juices down until it was syrupy and then mixed the tomatoes back in. Problem solved--no runny filling. Sliced perfectly with no mess. It was very sweet, so I might try cutting back the sugar next time. This is a great way to use up green tomatoes.

Fantastic, I loved this pie. I doubled the recipe using 6 cups of unpeeled sliced green tomatoes and used small instant tapioca instead of flour. I went really heavy on the cinnamon and I added 1/2- 1 tsp nutmeg. The next time I make it I will up the tomatoes to 8 cups and make 2 deep dish pies. Note: 2 tsp instant tapioca equals 1 TBLSP flour. Using Tapioca and a gluten free crust would make this a GF pie.

I made it as a cobbler or crumble, with no pie crust and a crumble topping (3/4 cup flour, 1/4 cup sugar, 3-4 tbsp butter), and it turned out great. My kids said it was the best thing I've ever made. If you think of it as a cobbler, it's the right texture.

For any green tomato pie recipe, it helps to lightly salt the cut up tomatoes and drain in a colander for about 30 minutes before mixing with the other ingredients. Helps take out the extra juice so the pie is not so runny. I always add a bit more cornstarch or flour than the recipe calls for.

I made this pie today and it turned out to be a hit at the get together that I went to. I did, however, adjust it. I added about 1/2 tsp salt to the dry mixture, I used 1/2 cup of flour, and I dotted the top with 2 Tbsp butter before putting the top crust on and last I baked it at 425 degrees F for 45 minutes. Baking time could vary from 35-45 minutes. The pie is done when the top is golden brown and the juices are bubbling out of the top. Hope you are as successful as I was.

My grandma and aunts used to make green tomato pie every year, so this recipe brings back fond memories from childhood. It's one of those old fashioned ways to make the most of everything you got from the garden. I had more success when I baked at 425. I also sliced the tomatoes like I would slice apples for apple pie. Then sprinkled the top crust with extra cinnamon sugar. YUM!

I made some changes but I really love this recipe. First change I made as suggested was to increase the amount of flour to 1/3 C. and I used 2 tsp of cinnamon. My favorite recipe for pie crust was only for a single crust so I topped this with a dutch crumble topping. OMG sooo good.

What a great thing to do with all those green tomatos at the end of the season. I peeled and deseeded the tomatoes and cut them up fairly fine. I also used the mature green tomatos as one person recommented. I did add a good 1/2 cup flour because others said to do that. Next time I will cut the tomatoes even finer. I think a food processor would work. The flavor was perfect. I also cut the sugar back to a strong 1 cup. I will make again every fall.

I think the directions should be rearranged. Sometimes getting the crust ready in the pan takes a while. I bought store crusts which are round and rerolled them for a square pan like in your photo. By the time I was finished, the coating on the tomatoes all ran off and there was a lot of liquid. I believe this is where the runny issue is coming from. My advice is to prepare your crust first. Then, right after you fold in the flour sugar mix and coat the tomatoes, put them directly in the pie plate. Cover with your top crust, solid or lattice, and bake as soon as possible. My first try is baking right now so we'll see what happens, but these are the things I know I would already change for next time. Thank you for your recipe!!
Not bad but if I ever make it again I’d cook the tomatoes a bit. They were pretty crunchy and it took away from what could be a decent pie

So a Google search of what to do with an excess of green tomatoes led me here. I was horrified. I was intrigued. I had already frozen all of my green tomatoes in chunks but with all the concerns about too much liquid and too hard tomatoes, I figured they would be perfect. Thawed and drained, there really wasn't much liquid. I followed quite a few suggestions from other comments, extended cooking time to about 50 minutes, added some cornstarch, and did an oatmeal streusal topping instead of a closed top crust. I made it for christmas and it came out great. One guest who had some the day I made it and another slice 3 days later said it was better after "aging" and I agree. I would make a day in advance in thr future to give the flavors time to mellow and meld. Will make again! Only 4 stars because of all the tweaks needed.
Soup. It’s been in the oven for an hour and still soupy.

This was amazing with a couple tweaks! Doubled the flour in the mix and added a generous few shakes of cayenne for some heat. I also chopped a medium vidalia onion into the tomato mix. I baked at 425 for 10min and then dropped to 350 for about 45min. Egg washed the lattice too. It’s sooooo good!

Easy to make, very running and impossible to serve. Tomatoes were crunchy. Wish I would have read the comments. Might try again and cook down the filling before putting it in the oven. I like the idea of adding tapioca.
Don't get me wrong it tasted very good just like apple pie, it was just very runny, next time definitely listening to the reviews
